best-mosquito-repellents-what-works-for-.title: Best Mosquito Repellents: What Works in a Mesa Backyard
best-mosquito-repellents-what-works-for-.content:
The best mosquito repellents are the ones that carry an EPA registration: DEET, picaridin, oil of lemon eucalyptus (or its synthetic form, PMD), IR3535 and 2-undecanone. Used on skin as the label directs, they give hours of protection, while candles, wristbands and ultrasonic gadgets do very little. If mosquitoes are still swarming your Mesa yard after you dump the water, call us at (480) 422-8388 or see our mosquito control in Mesa page.

Which Mosquito Repellents Actually Work?

Only the active ingredients that the EPA has evaluated for skin use have solid evidence behind them. The CDC points people to the same short list, and it is the list we tell Mesa homeowners to follow when they ask us what to buy at the store. The product name and the scent matter far less than the ingredient on the back of the bottle.

Active ingredientTypeHow it performsGood to know
DEETSyntheticLongest tested protection, rises with concentrationCan damage some plastics and synthetic fabrics
PicaridinSyntheticComparable to DEET at similar strengthNearly odorless and does not feel greasy
Oil of lemon eucalyptus / PMDPlant-basedGood protection, shorter than DEETThe EPA-registered form is not the same as plain lemon eucalyptus essential oil, and the label says not for children under three
IR3535SyntheticModerateGentle on skin, reapply more often
2-undecanonePlant-derivedModerateFound in some newer natural-style products

Is DEET safe to use on my family?

When used as directed, EPA-registered repellents are considered safe for adults and for children above the age on the label. Spray your hands and rub it on a child's face rather than spraying near the eyes and mouth, never put it under clothing or on cuts, and wash it off when you come inside. If you have questions about a baby or a pregnancy, ask your doctor.

Do natural repellents work as well?

Some do and many do not. Registered plant-based ingredients such as PMD hold up in testing, but a bottle of "essential oil blend" that has no EPA registration has not been tested the same way. Look for the EPA registration number on the label.

Which Mosquito Products Do Not Work?

Several popular products have little or no evidence behind them, and Mesa homeowners often buy them first because they sit by the register at the store. Skip these or treat them as a small extra:

  • Ultrasonic repellers and phone apps: studies have found they do not reduce bites.
  • Wristbands and clip-on devices: they protect only a tiny area around the band.
  • Vitamin B and garlic supplements: there is no reliable evidence that eating them keeps mosquitoes away.
  • Bug zappers: they kill mostly harmless insects, not the mosquitoes biting you.
  • Citronella candles: they add a small amount of smoke and scent, but they do not make a patio mosquito-free.

The same goes for backyard plants. We covered that in our post on plants that prevent mosquitoes, and the short version is that herbs help a little, not a lot.

How Long Does Each Repellent Last in Mesa Heat?

Less than the label suggests on a hot day. Sweat, swimming and a 105-degree afternoon all wear repellent off the skin faster, so reapply based on the label and use the heavier end of the protection range when you are outside for hours. In the cooler evenings of October through April, a single application tends to carry you much further.

What is the best way to apply it?

Put sunscreen on first, then repellent on top. Cover all exposed skin, including ankles and the backs of the neck and ears, which are the spots mosquitoes find first. Use only enough to cover the skin, and do not spray indoors in a closed room.

Can I treat my clothes too?

Yes. Permethrin is registered for treating clothing, shoes and camping gear, but never for use on skin. Treat items outdoors, let them dry fully, and follow the label.

Why Do Mosquitoes Bother Mesa Yards So Much?

Because Mesa is full of irrigated ground in a desert. Flood-irrigated lawns, canal laterals, neighborhood retention basins, and the green spaces around Riverview Park and Red Mountain keep water on the surface long after a monsoon storm has passed. Mosquitoes need only a bottle cap of water to breed, so a leaking drip valve in 85203 can feed a yard the same way a pond does.

Two groups cause most of the trouble. Culex mosquitoes breed in stagnant water and bite at dusk, while Aedes mosquitoes breed in small containers and bite in the daytime. Both can be active in Mesa from spring through the fall monsoon months, with the heaviest pressure from July through October. We talk more about that rhythm in our guide to stopping mosquitoes in the 85208 area of Mesa.

What Should You Do Around the House Besides Using Repellent?

Remove the water they breed in, because repellent protects only you while the mosquitoes keep multiplying a few feet away. A mosquito can go from egg to biting adult in about a week in Valley heat, so a once-a-week walk around the yard is the habit that makes the biggest difference. Check these spots first:

  1. Plant saucers, buckets, toys and anything else that holds water.
  2. Bird baths and pet bowls, which need scrubbing and refilling every few days.
  3. Drip irrigation valve boxes and low spots where water sits after watering.
  4. Gutters, rain barrels and the lids of covered containers after a storm.
  5. Swimming pools, fountains and spas that are no longer circulating.

Then add a layer of comfort. A fan on the patio does more than most people expect, because mosquitoes are weak fliers and have trouble reaching you in moving air. Sit away from dense shrubs and ivy, where mosquitoes rest in the shade during the day.

What should I do after I get bitten?

Wash the bite with soap and water and avoid scratching, since broken skin invites infection. A cold compress or an over-the-counter anti-itch product usually settles the itch. Mosquitoes in Arizona can carry West Nile virus, so let a doctor know if a fever, a severe headache or body aches follow a stretch of bites.

Does repellent matter in the cooler months?

Less, but it still counts. Mild Mesa evenings from October into November keep people outside and keep mosquitoes biting until the first real cold snap. Keep a bottle by the back door so it is there when you need it, and keep dumping standing water until the weather turns.

Repellent or Yard Treatment: Which Do You Need?

Repellent protects the person, and a yard treatment reduces the mosquitoes in the area. Most Mesa families end up using both during the worst months.

SituationBest approach
A hike, a ball game or a quick trip outsideEPA-registered repellent on skin
Occasional bites on the patioDump water weekly, run a fan, wear repellent at dusk
Bitten the moment you step outsideLook for hidden water, then call a professional
Daytime biting under shade treesA professional treatment of the resting areas
A neighbor's pool or a nearby basin is the sourceRepellent plus a professional yard treatment

A professional visit finds the breeding spots you cannot see, such as a covered valve box or a clogged drain, and treats the places where adult mosquitoes rest. If you are in Mesa, we cover neighborhoods across 85201 through 85215 and the surrounding East Valley.

Do You Also Service Cities Near Mesa?

Yes, and the mosquito picture is similar across the East Valley. See our mosquito pages for Gilbert, Chandler, Tempe and Queen Creek, or head to the pest control in Mesa overview for everything we handle. When you are ready, you can request service online.

What Else Should Mesa Homeowners Read?

  • Monsoon mosquitoes in Gilbert explains what summer storms do to breeding.
  • How long mosquitoes live covers the life cycle behind the weekly water check.
  • Fruit flies and gnats helps if what you have are not true mosquitoes.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best mosquito repellent for kids?

Choose an EPA-registered product whose label allows use on children, such as picaridin or DEET at a moderate strength. Do not use oil of lemon eucalyptus on children under three, apply it to your own hands first, and keep it away from the eyes and mouth.

What is the best mosquito repellent for a patio or yard?

Repellent on skin works best for people, and a fan plus weekly water removal works best for the space. Spatial products like candles and coils give only a small area of relief, so do not rely on them for a whole yard.

How often should I reapply mosquito repellent in Arizona heat?

Follow the label, and reapply sooner if you are sweating heavily or have been in the pool. Heat and sweat shorten the protection time, especially in the summer months.

Do mosquito repellents work on Aedes mosquitoes that bite in the daytime?

Yes. EPA-registered repellents work on both Culex and Aedes mosquitoes, so use them whenever you are outside, not just at dusk.

Why do mosquitoes seem to bite me more than other people?

Mosquitoes follow carbon dioxide, body heat and skin chemistry, and those differ from person to person. That is why one person on the patio gets bitten while another is left alone, and why repellent matters even if you feel you are not a target.

Can you treat my Mesa yard for mosquitoes?

Yes. We service Mesa and have been serving Arizona homeowners since 2013. Call (480) 422-8388 or request service online.

can-cockroaches-fly-what-maricopa-homeow.title: Cockroaches That Can Fly: What Maricopa Homeowners Should Know
can-cockroaches-fly-what-maricopa-homeow.content:
Yes, some cockroaches can fly. In Maricopa the flyers are almost always American cockroaches, the big reddish-brown roaches many people call palmetto bugs, and smokybrown cockroaches. They fly short, clumsy distances when it is warm, when they are startled, or when they are drawn to a light. A flying roach in your house means they are getting in or breeding nearby.

Which Cockroaches Can Fly in Maricopa, AZ?

Most of the roaches people find indoors do not fly at all. German cockroaches have wings but almost never use them, and they tend to run for cover instead. The flyers we see around 85138 and 85139 come from two groups.

  • American cockroaches are the largest common house roach, usually 1.5 to 2 inches long, reddish brown with a pale yellowish band behind the head. They are the ones that glide through an open garage door at dusk.
  • Smokybrown cockroaches are slightly smaller, dark and glossy, and they are strong fliers that come to porch lights and patio lights at night.
  • Wood roaches and other outdoor species sometimes fly into homes near landscaping, especially at night, but they usually do not set up an indoor colony.

The common thread is size. Large winged roaches are outdoor and sewer-dwelling insects that wander inside, which is a different problem from the small German roach infestation that lives in a kitchen. If you want to compare, our Mesa guide to getting rid of German cockroaches covers the small kitchen roach.

How Do You Tell a Flying Roach From Other Flying Bugs?

A roach has a flat, oval body, long whip-like antennae and six spiny legs. Beetles and palo verde beetles in Maricopa look similar at a glance, but they have hard wing covers that meet in a straight line down the back and shorter antennae. Roaches have flatter, softer-looking wings that overlap.

InsectTypical sizeColorAntennaeWhere you usually see it
American cockroach1.5 to 2 inchesReddish brown with a light band behind the headLong, thinGarages, drains, block walls, patios at night
Smokybrown cockroach1 to 1.5 inchesDark glossy brownLong, thinAround lights, trees, roof edges
German cockroachAbout half an inchLight tan with two dark stripesLong, thinKitchens and bathrooms
Palo verde beetle2 to 3 inchesDark brown, hard shellShort, thickNear palo verde trees, summer evenings

Why Do Cockroaches Fly at Night in Maricopa?

Roaches fly when conditions favor it. Warm evenings, humidity after a monsoon storm and bright outdoor lighting all push American and smokybrown roaches to take off. They usually glide down from a wall or a tree rather than flying in a straight line, which is why one can seem to land on you out of nowhere.

Their flight is more of a controlled glide than steady flying. A roach will often launch from a wall, a tree trunk or a roofline and drift down toward the ground or the nearest light, then run for cover when it lands. In a neighborhood with block walls, mature landscaping and lit patios, there are plenty of launch points and plenty of places to land.

Does the heat make roaches fly more?

Warm weather makes them more active and more willing to fly. A long Arizona summer means that window runs for many months in Maricopa, and warm evenings can stretch into the fall.

Why do roaches come toward porch lights?

Smokybrown roaches in particular are drawn to light at night. A bright porch fixture near a door pulls them to the exact spot where they can slip inside when you open it.

Why Are Roaches Getting Into Maricopa Homes?

Maricopa is a young, fast-growing city, and many neighborhoods such as Rancho El Dorado, Province, Glennwilde, Tortosa and Cobblestone Farms sit on newer sewer lines, block walls and irrigated landscaping. Those are exactly the conditions American cockroaches prefer, because they live in sewers, storm drains and damp planter beds and come up to find food and water.

  • Sewer and drain access. We cover this in detail in our guide to sewer roaches in Maricopa.
  • Gaps around garage doors. A worn bottom seal is an open invitation for a large roach.
  • Irrigated landscaping. Damp mulch, leaf litter and thick groundcover give roaches shade and moisture right against the house, and overgrown beds are a harbor in the same way weeds are. Good weed and lawn care in Maricopa keeps these edges clean.
  • Block walls and wall voids. Roaches travel along the walls between yards, and the gaps at expansion joints and utility penetrations let them in.
  • Stored boxes and clutter. Cardboard in a garage gives them a place to hide during the day.

Is a Flying Cockroach a Sign of an Infestation?

It depends on how often it happens and where you see it. Timing matters: a roach in the garage after a monsoon storm is a different story from a roach on the kitchen counter at noon.

One flying roach on a hot night is not always an infestation, but it is a signal. If you see a single large roach once, it may have wandered in. If you see several in a week, or you see them in the daytime, they are living close to the house or inside it.

What does a roach infestation look like?

Look for droppings that resemble coffee grounds or black pepper, shed skins, egg cases and a musty smell. American cockroach egg cases are dark, bean-shaped capsules often found in hidden damp spots.

Are flying roaches dangerous?

They do not sting, but they walk through sewers, drains and garbage and then across your counters. Roaches are linked to allergy and asthma triggers, so get them under control rather than just swatting the ones you see. If you are wondering whether they can bite, read our guide on whether cockroaches bite.

How Do You Keep Flying Roaches Out of Your House?

You can cut down on roach entries. Do these first, and then bring in a professional for anything that keeps coming back.

  1. Replace worn garage door seals and weatherstrip exterior doors so there is no daylight at the bottom.
  2. Switch to yellow or warm LED bulbs near entry doors, or move bright lights away from the door itself, so they pull fewer night fliers to your threshold.
  3. Seal gaps around pipes, vents, cables and where block walls meet the slab.
  4. Cover floor drains and run water in rarely used sinks and tubs so the traps stay full.
  5. Pull mulch back a few inches from the foundation and clear leaf piles and wet debris near the house.
  6. Store boxes in plastic bins instead of cardboard in the garage.
  7. Fix leaks and wipe up standing water under sinks, because roaches need water more than food.

If you have a pool, a drip irrigation system or a lot of potted plants, you already have more moisture around the house than a typical desert yard, and that is worth checking first when roaches show up. Pool equipment pads, irrigation boxes and water meter boxes are common hiding spots close to the house.

Do Store-Bought Roach Sprays Work on Flying Roaches?

A spray kills the roach it touches and not much else. Large roaches live in sewers, wall voids and landscaping, so a can of spray on the kitchen floor does not reach the source. Repellent sprays can also push roaches deeper into walls, and a baited approach works better for the small species. For large outdoor roaches, treating the exterior perimeter and the entry points is what actually reduces how many reach your door.

What Does Professional Roach Control Look Like in Maricopa?

We start with an inspection of the garage, the kitchen, the bathrooms, the exterior perimeter, the block walls and the landscaping. Then we treat the places where roaches enter and hide, tell you what to change around the home, and follow up to make sure the activity drops. Our roach elimination service in Maricopa is built around finding how they are getting in, not just treating what you can see. Roaches rarely come alone, and the same moisture and cracks that let one in can let other pests in too. If you are also seeing bites at night, check our bed bug treatment in Maricopa page, since people sometimes confuse the two.

We have been serving Arizona homeowners since 2013, and our Maricopa pest and termite technicians work on homes across Maricopa every week.

Yes. Roaches do not stop at the city line, and neither do we. Besides Maricopa we service homeowners in Casa Grande, Chandler, Queen Creek, Gilbert and Phoenix. Here are the local pages for the neighbors closest to Maricopa:

Frequently Asked Questions

Can cockroaches really fly?

Yes. American and smokybrown cockroaches can fly, usually for short distances and mostly when it is warm. German cockroaches have wings but almost never fly.

Are palmetto bugs the same as cockroaches?

Yes. Palmetto bug is a nickname for a large cockroach, most often the American cockroach. They are the same insect.

Why is a huge cockroach flying around my Maricopa house at night?

It is most likely an American or smokybrown roach drawn to your lights on a warm night. It came from the sewer, a drain, landscaping or a block wall, so look for how it got in.

Will a flying roach hurt me or my pets?

It will not sting you. It can spread bacteria across surfaces and trigger allergies, so clean up and deal with the entry point.

How do I get rid of flying roaches in my garage?

Replace the door seal, seal the gaps, store things in plastic bins and cut the moisture. If the roaches keep coming, call us for an inspection.

what-does-a-scorpion-sting-look-like-wha.title: What Does a Scorpion Sting Look Like? What Avondale Homeowners Should Know
what-does-a-scorpion-sting-look-like-wha.content:
A bark scorpion sting usually looks like very little: a tiny puncture or a faint pink spot, sometimes no mark at all. The sting is recognized by how it feels, with sharp burning pain, tingling and numbness that spread past the spot. If you were stung in Avondale and symptoms go beyond the sting site, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 right away.

This guide is general information about pests, not medical advice. For a sting that worries you, call Poison Control or a doctor, and call 911 for trouble breathing or swallowing.

What Does a Scorpion Sting Look Like on the Skin?

Most Arizona scorpion stings come from the bark scorpion, the small, pale tan scorpion that is common across the West Valley. Its venom works on the nerves, so the pain is out of proportion to what you can see. The skin often looks normal.

  • Little or no visible mark. You may see one tiny puncture, or nothing at all.
  • Mild redness or a small swollen spot. It is usually the size of a coin or smaller.
  • No big blister or spreading bruise. A sting that blisters, oozes or spreads in a widening red area is more likely a different bite, such as a spider or an infection setting in.

The better test is the feeling, not the look. Lightly tapping the area often makes the pain flare, a classic sign of a bark scorpion sting.

What Does a Scorpion Sting Feel Like?

Expect sudden, sharp, burning pain, like a hot needle. Within minutes you may feel pins and needles or numbness that moves up the arm, leg, foot or hand. Many people describe a strange "electric" feeling. The sting site may be sensitive to the touch of a sheet or a sock.

What you noticeTypical for a bark scorpion sting?What to do
Tiny puncture or no markYes, very commonWash the area and call Poison Control for guidance
Sharp burning pain, pain when tappedYesCool compress, keep the limb still, call Poison Control
Tingling or numbness near the stingYesWatch closely and call Poison Control
Numbness or tingling spreading far from the stingCan happenCall Poison Control or a doctor now
Trouble swallowing, drooling, restless eye or muscle movement, trouble breathingA serious reactionCall 911
Large blister, spreading redness, pusNo, may be another bite or infectionSee a doctor

What Should You Do Right After a Scorpion Sting?

Stay calm and follow these steps. Poison Control in Arizona is free, staffed around the clock, and used to scorpion calls.

  1. Wash the sting site with soap and water.
  2. Apply a cool, damp cloth to the area. Do not put ice directly on the skin.
  3. Keep the stung arm or leg still and at about heart level.
  4. Call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 and describe your symptoms.
  5. Take a photo of the scorpion if you can do it safely, or catch it in a jar, to confirm what stung you.

What should you not do after a scorpion sting?

Do not cut the skin, try to suck out venom, or use a tourniquet. None of it helps and some of it does harm. Do not put the stung limb in ice water, and do not give a small child any medicine until you have talked with Poison Control or a doctor. If the sting happened at night, do not just go back to sleep and hope it fades, because the symptoms you most need to catch can appear in the first hour or two.

Who should be seen quickly?

Young children, older adults and anyone with other health problems should be checked promptly. Children can have strong reactions, so do not wait to see if it passes.

How long does a scorpion sting last?

Pain and numbness commonly last for hours and can come and go for a day or more. A doctor or Poison Control can tell you what is normal for the person stung.

Why Are There Scorpions in Avondale, AZ?

Avondale sits on the Agua Fria River in the West Valley, with older neighborhoods around Historic Avondale and newer subdivisions across 85323 and 85392 such as Garden Lakes, Coldwater Springs and Rancho Santa Fe. Bark scorpions can live anywhere in that mix, and a few local features help them.

  • Block walls. Bark scorpions climb. They rest in the gaps and cap blocks of the walls between yards.
  • Irrigated landscaping. Damp mulch, rock beds and thick groundcover hold the insects scorpions eat, such as crickets and roaches.
  • River corridors and open desert edges. Land along the Agua Fria and the edge of the Estrella foothills sends scorpions toward new construction as it develops.
  • Stucco and door gaps. A scorpion can flatten itself to squeeze through a gap about the thickness of a credit card.

Scorpions are most active at night, mostly in the warm months, and they tend to be seen more after a monsoon storm drives them out of their hiding spots.

When are scorpions most active around Avondale homes?

Activity picks up as nights warm in spring and stays high through summer and into the fall. Evenings after the monsoon storms of July through September are a common time for a surprise sting, because the rain and humidity push scorpions and their prey out into the open. Most stings happen indoors at night: bare feet on a tile floor, a hand reaching into a shoe or a laundry pile, or a child rolling over onto one in bed.

How Do You Tell a Scorpion Sting From a Spider Bite?

A scorpion sting hurts immediately and sharply, with tingling and numbness. A spider bite is often painless at first and may show a red area, swelling or a blister hours later. If you saw the creature, a scorpion has pincers and a curled tail with a stinger. Our spider prevention in Avondale page covers the spiders people mix up with scorpions at the sting site.

How Do You Stop Scorpions From Getting Into an Avondale Home?

You will never remove every scorpion from the desert, but you can make your house a poor target.

Seal the entry points

Replace worn weatherstripping on the garage and entry doors, caulk gaps around pipes and cables, and close the gaps where block walls meet the house.

Cut off their food and shelter

Scorpions follow their prey. Controlling crickets, roaches and other bugs removes the reason they come near your walls. Move firewood, rock piles and stacked pots away from the house, and trim shrubs back from the stucco.

Check at night with a blacklight

Scorpions glow under a UV flashlight. A walk around the yard and block walls after dark shows you where they travel. Our technicians use the same blacklight method, then seal and treat the perimeter.

Shake it out

Shake out shoes, towels and clothes left on the floor or in the garage, and check bedding for kids who sleep near a wall.

What Does Professional Scorpion Control in Avondale Include?

Our scorpion control in Avondale program is built around finding how they get in. A technician walks the property, inspects with a blacklight, treats the perimeter and gaps, and works on the pests scorpions feed on. It is part of our Avondale pest and termite service for homes across Avondale. We have served Arizona homeowners since 2013.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does a scorpion sting look like?

Often like almost nothing. A bark scorpion sting may leave a tiny puncture or slight redness. Pain, tingling and numbness are the main signs.

Does a scorpion sting leave a mark?

Sometimes a small pink or red spot, but many stings leave no visible mark. A big blister or spreading redness points to something else.

When should I go to the ER for a scorpion sting?

Call 911 for trouble breathing or swallowing, drooling, or unusual eye or muscle movements. Children and older adults should be checked promptly, so call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 first.

Are all scorpions in Arizona dangerous?

The bark scorpion is the one that matters most. Other Arizona scorpions, such as the giant desert hairy scorpion, tend to cause milder stings, but treat any sting seriously and call for advice.

How do I keep scorpions out of my Avondale house?

Seal door and wall gaps, remove clutter and the bugs they eat, and have the perimeter treated. A blacklight check at night shows where they travel.
